## Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — DESKTOP-B8TQK49

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, 2024-11-26 08:49:38 to 09:43:58 UTC+4) and the accompanying Suricata alert export (`...-alerts.txt`).

### Victim host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Source of all malicious traffic below |
| MAC | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183`) and Ethernet source on all frames from .183 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS registration (`<00>`/`<20>` records) and NetBIOS "Host Announcement" browser frame |
| AD domain / DC | `nemotodes.health`, DC **NEMOTODES-DC** (10.11.26.3) | SMB2 tree connects to `\\NEMOTODES-DC.nemotodes.health\IPC$`, `\sysvol`, `\Shared_Files` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | `kerberos.CNameString` in TGS/AS-REQ traffic from 10.11.26.183 to the DC |

### Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client/protocol, weaponized for unauthorized remote access) — **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral. Confirmation is two-fold:

1. **Suricata signatures fired repeatedly** (from the alert export): `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (x65), `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (x2), `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` (x65), `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response` (x4), `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
2. **Literal protocol strings observed in cleartext HTTP** when following TCP stream 77 (10.11.26.183:53362 → 194.180.191.64:443): the client sends `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, the server replies `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`, and the bodies use the exact NetSupport client-gateway command grammar (`CMD=POLL` / `INFO=1` / `ACK=1` for check-ins, `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<binary>` for encrypted C2 payloads).

### Infection chain (timeline, UTC+4)

- **08:50:11** — DNS resolves `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5), followed at 08:50:14–08:50:16 by `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) and `createsend1.com` (Campaign Monitor CDN). These look like a redirect/landing chain but were **not independently alerted** — listed as unconfirmed context, not a hard IOC.
- **08:50:14 – 08:50:40** — DNS resolves **modandcrackedapk.com → 193.42.38.139**, and the host opens two TLS sessions to it with SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`. Suricata flagged both the DNS lookup and the TLS SNI as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain` (a known cracked-software/mod-APK lure domain). This is the most likely payload-delivery point; the payload itself is inside encrypted TLS application data, so no dropped file could be recovered from the capture.
- **08:50:45** — Host queries `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231), `GET /location/loca.asp`, receiving back `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta-area geolocation). This is NetSupport RAT's own built-in geolocation self-check, run immediately before C2 starts.
- **08:50:45 onward, continuously through end of capture** — Repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1` to **194.180.191.64:443** (plain HTTP on port 443, not TLS), carrying the NetSupport POLL/ENCD check-in protocol described above. 132 frames / ~24 KB observed in this single conversation across the capture (`conv,ip` for 194.180.191.64), spanning ~3164 seconds — sustained C2 beaconing, not a one-off.

### Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| c2_endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** | Sustained `POST /fakeurl.htm` beacons with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)`; matches `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`/`CnC Checkin` alerts |
| url | `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` | Literal POST target in every C2 beacon (tcp.stream 77 and dozens of subsequent streams) |
| domain | **modandcrackedapk.com** (resolved to 193.42.38.139) | DNS query + TLS ClientHello SNI at 08:50:14/08:50:40; matches `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI` |
| domain | geo.netsupportsoftware.com (104.26.1.231) | `GET /location/loca.asp` immediately preceding first C2 check-in; matches `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`. This is NetSupport's own legitimate infrastructure being called by the malicious client — a behavioral fingerprint of the RAT, not a separate attacker server |
| url | `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` | Frame 20336, response body `33.7488,-84.3877` |

**File names / SHA256 hashes:** none could be grounded in the capture. The likely payload delivery occurs inside TLS-encrypted sessions to 193.42.38.139 (no decryption keys available), and the ongoing C2 channel uses NetSupport's own `ENCD` obfuscation over plaintext HTTP rather than a file transfer — no executable, installer, or document was observed in the clear.

### Benign context (do not treat as IOCs)

- Extensive SAMR/DRSUAPI/LSARPC/NETLOGON RPC calls from 10.11.26.183 to the DC (10.11.26.3) at 08:49:55 are routine Windows domain-logon/group-policy queries. The `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt`, `Potentially unsafe SMBv1 protocol in use`, and `[MS-EFSR] EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` alerts are well-known false-positive triggers on ordinary domain-joined SMB/RPC traffic — no exploitation indicators were observed alongside them.
- Standard Windows/Office/Edge telemetry and update traffic: `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `login.live.com`, Adobe ARM check-ins (`acroipm2.adobe.com`), Google/Bing services, `code.jquery.com`, `r10.o.lencr.org` (OCSP) — normal enterprise workstation background noise.
- `classicgrand.com`, `confirmsubscription.com`, `createsend1.com` — resolved just before the malicious domain but not themselves flagged by any signature; plausibly part of the redirect/ad chain leading to `modandcrackedapk.com`, but not confirmed malicious on their own.

### Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged on as domain user **oboomwald** in the `nemotodes.health` domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after browsing to the cracked-software lure domain **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) around 08:50 UTC+4. Within seconds the host began sustained, signature-confirmed NetSupport RAT command-and-control beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** via repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm` requests bearing the literal `NetSupport Manager/1.3` client and `NetSupport Gateway/1.8` server identifiers, continuing for the remainder of the capture.
